title: Rich Grenadine
directions: This is based on using a 500ml bottle for storage. Adjust amounts accordingly.
Pour juice into the sauce pan and heat on low to medium
After a few minutes, add the sugar and stir regularly
Once sugar is fully integrated, stir in molasses, remove from the heat and let cool to room temp
Stir in blossom water, funnel into bottle and enjoy!
The 2.5:1.5 ratio helps keep the solution shelf stable. Adjust recipe according to taste. Or go 1:1, refrigerate and be careful of spoilage.

title: 5:1 Saline Solution
directions: Pour juice into the sauce pan, add salt and heat on medium
Stir regularly until salt is fully integrated
Remove from the heat and let cool to room temp
Funnel into bottle and enjoy!

title: Rich Simple Syrup
directions: This is based on using a 250ml bottle for storage. Adjust amounts accordingly.
Pour water into the sauce pan and heat on low to medium
After a little steam starts rising, slowly add the sugar and stir regularly
After the solution becomes clear (relative to sugar color) remove from the heat and let cool to room temp
Strain and funnel solution into bottle and enjoy!
notes: The 2:1 ratio keeps the solution shelf stable. Or go 1.5:1 or 1:1, refrigerate and be careful of spoilage.
Don't let it come to a boil. Some water will evaporate, so exact amounts will vary.

title: Rich Demerara Syrup
directions: This is based on using a 250ml bottle for storage. Adjust amounts accordingly.
Pour water into the sauce pan and heat on low to medium
After a little steam starts rising, slowly add the sugar and stir regularly
After the solution becomes clear (relative to sugar color) remove from the heat and let cool to room temp
Strain and funnel solution into bottle and enjoy!
notes: The 2:1 ratio keeps the solution shelf stable. Or go 1.5:1 or 1:1, refrigerate and be careful of spoilage.
Don't let it come to a boil. Some water will evaporate, so exact amounts will vary.

title: Rich Honey Syrup
directions: This is based on using a 250ml bottle for storage. Adjust amounts accordingly.
Pour honey into into the sauce pan at low to medium heat
Add water and stir regularly
Do not let it come to a boil.
After the solution appears integrated, remove from the heat and let cool to room temp
Strain and funnel solution into bottle and enjoy!

title: Caipirinha
directions: Start with a double rocks glass
Cut ends off lime, then in half, then into 8ths and put in glass
Add sugar and muddle until well mixed, then add Cachaca
Fill rest of the glass with crushed ice
Stir and enjoy! Saúde!
notes: The Caipirinha is the national drink of Brazil.
The history is murky, but it appears to have been around by at least the 1850s.
One story credits creation by a farmer as a fancy celebratory cocktail, another suggests is was a medicinal concoktail.

directions: Chill glass

Drop in ice, stir to chill, add twist and enjoy! Saúde!
notes: The origins with variations of this date back to the 1950s.
Cynar is the registered official Amaro, but it can vary.
In 2023, this drink was officially recognized by the International Bartenders Association.

title: Daiquiri
directions: Chill glass

Fill large shaker with ice, roll in the liquids and shake til cold
Double strain into glass and enjoy!
notes: Credit for this classic goes back to 1898 and Jennings Cox, an engineer working in the mining town of Daiquiri, Cuba.
While he gets all the credit, logic and the prevelance of the three ingredients suggests the combination must have existed prior.
His original creation ended with the ingredients in an ice filled glass, kind of in between the classic cocktail served up and the party favorite, frozen daiquiri.
About 10 years later, Admiral Lucious Johnson visited the town, discovered the drink, and brought it back to the U.S. where its popularity took off.

A 1651 document in Barbados referred to rum as 'Kill-Devil', saying it was a hot, hellish and terrible liquor.

Muddle sugar to spread out across bottom of the glass
Drop in ice cube then pour over the whiskey and stir
Dash in bitters, twist and drop in the orange peel, add the cherry and enjoy!
notes: Back in the early 1800s, the term cocktail was defined as, "a potent concoction of spirits, bitters, water, and sugar."
As time moved on and bartenders were experimenting with all sorts of mixtures, some ended up asking for their drink, the old-fashioned way.
It was at this point that whiskey was generally accepted as the defacto spirit, more notably, rye.

notes: Kamikaze, by definition, means 'divine wind' in Japanese.
The drink was thought to have been created at an American Naval Base, shortly after World War II.
It gained popularity in the 70s and 80s when shot culture really took hold.

title: Bloody Mary ... Gone Rogue
ingredients: 3 (or more) drops High River Rogue hot sauce
directions: Put lemon juice, Worcestershire, vodka, tomato juice, hot sauce, pepper and celery salt in shaker
Slowly roll between shaker cup 4-5 times ending in the small tin
Add ice cubes to small tin til almost full, connect to large tin and very slowly roll 4-5 times
Pour all contents into the glass, add 2 barspoons of horseradish and slowly stir up with bar spoon
Add skewered olives, straw and enjoy!
notes: One can elevate this a touch by giving the glass a celery salt rim.
This is a classic Bloody Mary recipe, just specifically named due to the use of the great Rogue hot sauce.
This drink goes back to Harry's American Bar in Paris in the 1920, thanks to barman Fernand Petiot.
The name is believed to come from a regular who said the drink reminded him of Mary, a bartender at Chicago's Bucket of Blood.

directions: Fill glass about 3/4 with ice

Slowly pour milk over back of the spoon to create the top layer
Give a gentle little stir to create a cloudy look and enjoy!
notes: This beverage was another creation from the 1970s sweet dessert cocktail craze.

notes: Thoughts are that this drink fast followed the Black Russian around 1949 in Brussels, Belgium.
There is some contradictory beliefs that it actually came about 5 years later in Oakland, California.

title: Ward 8
directions: Chill glass

Double strain into glass, add a wisp of cherry juice, garnish with 2 speared cherries and enjoy!
notes: This is believed to have been created in 1898 at the Locke-Ober Café in Boston.
It was crafted to celebrate the anticipated election victory of Martin M. Lomasney, who was running for a seat in the state legislature.
Apparently, Boston's Ward 8 was the district that consistently delivered Lomasney his winning margin.

Using a bar spoon, stir briefly and lift some mint up the glass a bit
Fill to the top of the glass with seltzer
Add straw, mint spring to garnish and enjoy!
notes: There's some great stories out there that Sir Francis Drake and crew pirated their way to the mojito origin, but there's no solid proof to back that up.
It's believe to have originated out of Cuba, and most likely, it was another mixture used for medicinal purposed, particularly to prevent scurvy.
It wasn't until the 1930s that the drink appeared in print and represented the fine drink we know and love today.

It's said that bartender Mirko Stocchetto accidentally swapped gin for prosecco while making a classic Negroni, and the resulting drink was quite tasty.

Fill will ice, seltzer and stir
Add orange twist and enjoy!
notes: This beverage originated out of Milan, Italy in the 1860s by Gaspare Campari.
It was originally named Milano-Torino after it's main ingredients.
Belief is that it changed names due to its popularity with American ex-pats some of who brought it back to the States around prohibition using a medicinal loophole.
This beverage is the precurser to the hugely popular cocktail, the Negroni.
The Americano was the first ever James Bond drink order, in the first novel, Casino Royale.

title: Gin and Tonic
directions: Stack ice in glass add gin and fill with tonic
Squeeze in some lime, add wedge to edge of glass and enjoy!
notes: British soldiers drank quinine heavy tonic to combat maleria, specifically in India.
The men would then add their daily ration of gin to this to make it more palatable and enjoyable.
It gained traction in The States in the 1930s as tonic companies marketed it at the Chicago and NY World's Fair.

title: Gin Rickey
directions: Stack ice in glass
Squeeze in the lime, then drop lime shell in.
Add gin and top off with seltzer
Stir gently with bar spoon and enjoy!
notes: Back in the 1880s, Colonel Joseph "Joe" Rickey was a regular at Shoomaker's, a popular Washington, D.C. saloon that he eventually purchased.
Rickey reportedly enjoyed bourbon, ice and sparkling water. Bartender George Williamson is often credited with adding fresh lime juice, creating what became known as the Bourbon Rickey.
By the 1890s, gin had become the more popular base spirit. The Gin Rickey was documented in print by 1893 and became a widely enjoyed American cocktail.

Another says that Johnnie Solan was challenged to make a new drink, varied the Duplex cocktail and named it after a recent visit to the newly openend Bronx Zoo.

Grohusko was the head bartender at Baracca's Restaurant in Wall Street, and honored his Brooklynite boss with this drink.

It was suspected to originate in the late 1800s or early 1900s.

title: Espresso Martini
directions: Pour liquids into shaker and shake
Double strain into a chilled martini glass, add 3 coffee beans and enjoy!
notes: You need to go back to 1983 London to find the origin of this cocktail.
The story is that a young - soon to be famous - model entered Dick Bradsell's bar and ask for a drink that would wake her up and also !@#$ her up.
The three bean garnish is a nod to Italian Sambuca and represent health, wealth and happiness.

title: Martini
directions: Chill glass
Pour liquids into a mixing glass, add ice and stir for a good chill
Strain into the chilled glass, add lanced olives and enjoy!
notes: The martini goes back to the 1800s with no truly known origin.
It is generally believed that this drink evolved from another gin/vermouth cocktail, the Martinez.
Harry Johnson's 1888 book has the Martini as 2 or 3 dashes of gum syrup, 2 or 3 dashes of Boker's bitters, 1 dash curacao, and 1:1 of Old Tom gin and vermouth with a lemon peel
The 1912 Hoffman House Bartender's Guide shows a 1:1 vermouth to gin ratio with orange bitters and lemon twist.

notes: The Water Lily was created in 2007 by New York bartender Richard Boccato at Little Branch in Manhattan's West Village.

According to accounts of its creation, Georgette Moger-Petraske, a regular at the bar and the wife of influential bartender Sasha Petraske, asked Boccato to make her a drink using gin and violet syrup.
Boccato developed a cocktail combining gin, orange liqueur, lemon juice and violet flavoring. When it came time to name it, they chose Water Lily in reference to Georgette's middle name, Lillian.
